neet_che_u05_t03_1.working: Raoult's law gives p_total = p_A0 + (p_B0 - p_A0)x_B. This is linear in x_B, so the plot is a straight line joining p_A0 and p_B0.

neet_che_u05_t03_2.working: At x_B = 0, p = 120, so p_A0 = 120 mm Hg. At x_B = 1, p = 120 - 75 = 45, so p_B0 = 45 mm Hg.

neet_che_u05_t03_3.working: The slope equals p0 = 32 mm Hg. With x_solute = 0.10, x_solvent = 0.90, so p = 32 × 0.9 = 28.8 mm Hg.

neet_che_u05_t03_4.working: Ideal solution: linear (III). Positive deviation: maximum in vapour pressure, minimum boiling azeotrope (I). Negative deviation: minimum in vapour pressure, maximum boiling azeotrope (IV). Azeotrope: liquid and vapour have the same composition (II).

neet_che_u05_t03_5.working: A is true. B is false: a vapour pressure minimum gives a maximum boiling azeotrope. C is true. D is true. E is false: for negative deviation the curve lies below the ideal line.
